Subject: Dedicated capacity — post-call recap & proposed next steps

Thanks again for the call today — good alignment on goals and constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get your engineering team set up for a short pilot:

Summary from call:
- Goal: move FinApp's document-summarization pipeline to Redwood Dedicated for predictable latency during peak trading hours and to use embedding-based similarity + reranker for higher precision.
- Primary concerns: auth and control plane isolation, predictable autoscaling for nightly spikes, embedding indexing throughput, and safe tool-calling/structured output handling.

Action items / next steps (proposed):
1) SDK & auth: share SDK setup + service-account instructions (attached). Dev team to confirm whether they prefer API keys or service-account integration for Dedicated.
2) Routing & model pinning: we'll provide a sample routing policy to pin Llama-2-13B for low-latency endpoints and route heavier batch jobs to larger model variants.
3) Structured output & tool calling: enable tool-calling mode and provide tool manifest; recommend a canary route for production.
4) Embeddings & reranker: recommended batching approach for indexing + a small reranker stage to improve precision for top-k.
5) Autoscaling & capacity sizing: initial recommendation (provisional): start with 4-GPU pool (NVIDIA A100-equivalent), autoscale 2-8 GPUs, target sustained concurrency per GPU 8-12 for 13B models; tune based on P95 latency targets. See attached arch diagram + SLA draft.

Proposed immediate next step: technical sync with Aditya + your SRE to walk through service account setup and an initial load test. Are you available Wed 10am PT?

Attachments: [redwood-arch-diagram.pdf] [service-account-instructions.pdf] [dedicated-sla-draft.docx]

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — autoscaling, throughput & integration details

Hi Cassie — looping in details so your SRE/infra team has concrete guidance before the Wed sync. Long answer short: service-account short-lived tokens preferred for Dedicated; we've included runbook links and concrete sizing guidance below.

1) Auth & SDKs
- Recommended: service-account based auth with short-lived tokens minted via the control plane (token exchange). This avoids long-lived API keys and integrates with customer-managed KMS if you choose that deployment.
- SDKs: we support Python and Node official SDKs. Example flow: create service account in Redwood Console -> grant "dedicated.pool.runner" role -> download local key (encrypted) -> exchange for short-lived token via SDK. See attached service-account-instructions.pdf for step-by-step commands and example IAM bindings.

2) Embeddings batching & indexing
- For ~5M docs (avg 1k tokens), recommended approach: chunk documents to ~256-512 token pieces, run batched embed endpoint with batch size 512-2048 images/rows depending on memory. Expect about 1000-3000 docs/sec for optimized parallel batch workers on 8-16 vCPU machines when using our async batch endpoint; actual throughput depends on network and pre/postprocessing.
- For initial indexing run, consider reserving a short burst capacity on Dedicated (burst to 8 GPUs) to finish faster and then scale down. We'll provide a sample batching worker in the Drive link.

3) Concurrency & latency guidance
- Empirical numbers (13B model, A100-equivalent):
  - Single-request (1k tokens) median (P50): ~120-200ms per token generation baseline; end-to-end median latency ~350-500ms at low concurrency.
  - P95 at concurrency 8-12: expect P95 ~650-900ms for a 1k token request with streaming off; enable streaming to start seeing early partial responses.
- Concurrency per GPU: start with target 8 concurrency for baseline, tune to 12 if you need higher throughput and can accept slightly higher P95. For larger models (70B) concurrency drops to 1-3.

4) Autoscaling, queues & throughput sizing
- Suggested pilot pool: 4 GPUs; autoscale min=2 / max=8. Autoscaler policy: scale on sustained GPU utilization >65% and queue depth >50 requests for >30s.
- Queueing: use a short request queue (max_wait_ms ~2000) for low-latency endpoints; for batch jobs use a longer worker queue with async endpoints.
- Burst capacity: enable short-term burst (60-120s) to handle nightly indexing jobs. Configure a hard cap on tokens/sec to avoid overrun.

5) Structured output & tool-calling
- Pattern: enable tool-calling only on canary route; Redwood's runtime enforces an outbound allowlist on Dedicated (you can restrict DNS/IP egress). For added safety, run tool-calling in a sandboxed environment (no external egress) during early testing. Tool manifests are passed as JSON in the request; SDKs validate schemas locally.

Attachments & links:
- redwood-arch-diagram.pdf (arch + routing examples)
- service-account-instructions.pdf (step-by-step)
- dedicated-sla-draft.docx
- Sizing doc + sample worker: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C4D-example
- Internal engineering ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ENG-987
